text:
IncidentBot: 🚨 ALERT: streaming p99 latency SLO breach detected for model t-rex-3b in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. p99 spiked to ~3.2s. Auto-page to oncall. Link: https://internal.metrics/incident/3654321987

Maria G: I'm on it, pinging oncall (@Ashwin K). seeing streaming stalls on dashboards too.

Ashwin K: Picking this up. Quick ask: any customer-facing reports?

Customer Success: Yep — two customers (acme-inc, finlytics) reported timeouts on streaming endpoints ~10:11-10:16 UTC. They saw partial responses then stall.

Ashwin K: Ok. I'm opening traces for sampled requests. First glance: tail latency correlated with kv cache eviction bursts on a subset of shards.

Samir R: FWIW I've got a telemetry snapshot: p95 ~280ms -> stable, p99 ~3200ms -> blowup. Streaming stall rate up from 0.4% -> 6.8% over 10m. KV metrics: global evictions/sec jumped from ~150 -> 9k. Hot shards: shard-12, shard-21.

Ashwin K: Logs snippet from shard-12 around spike:

```
[2026-03-15T10:11:58Z] shard=12 evict_count=9123 prefill_hits=32 prefill_attempts=320 decode_hits=280 decode_misses=940 tail_latency_ms=1320
[2026-03-15T10:12:02Z] shard=12 kv_mem_pressure=0.92 queue_depth=87 streaming_active=124
```

Maria G: That prefill vs decode ratio looks off — prefill attempts are low relative to decode traffic. Could be fragmentation/eviction churn causing lots of decode misses and regen.

Ashwin K: Agree. Also seeing continuous-batching size drop for streaming sessions on those shards — suggests frequent KV invalidation, more decode work, tail stalls.

Jules P: Do we have a quick mitigation runbook? Options: 1) increase KV eviction threshold on affected shards, 2) reroute streaming traffic off hot shards, 3) disable prefill for streaming routes temporarily (so decode path is consistent), 4) fallback to smaller model variant for streaming.

Ashwin K: Trying option 1 and 2 in parallel. Increasing cache window for shard-12/21 by API, and initiating reroute for streaming routes out of eu-west-1 -> eu-north-1 for low-priority customers.

prod-ops-bot: Executing command:
```
opsctl shard update --id shard-12 --kv-evict-threshold 0.98 --apply 
opsctl shard update --id shard-21 --kv-evict-threshold 0.98 --apply
```

prod-ops-bot: Reroute started:
```
/runbook reroute --from-region eu-west-1 --to-region eu-north-1 --policy=fallback-lowmem --filter='route:streaming and priority:low'
```

Samir R: Also toggled a conservative change: lowered batch_size for streaming decoding on shards 12/21 to reduce peak decode CPU.

Ashwin K: Observed early telemetry: evictions/sec on shard-12 dropped from 9.1k -> 1.2k within ~90s after threshold bump. p99 across streaming lowered from 3.2s -> 1.1s in ~6 minutes. Streaming stall rate down to 1.5%.

Customer Success: letting acme-inc and finlytics know — they reported improvement, still watching.

Maria G: Good. Root-cause signal: KV cache fragmentation + aggressive eviction under transient load (likely seq-len variance) caused prefill miss ratio to spike, which amplified decode latency and produced streaming tail stalls. Prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill hitrate dropped from ~80% -> 10% on hot shards.

Jules P: For next steps during handoff: keep reroute and increased thresholds active for 1hr while we continue to monitor. Need an in-depth postmortem: dataset of per-shard eviction patterns, sequence length distributions, prefix reuse rates, and a replay on staging to reproduce. Also evaluate smarter prefill gating when eviction churn is high.

Ashwin K: Handoff to Jules (next oncall) at 10:23 UTC. Summary for handoff:
- Incident: streaming p99 SLO breach due to KV eviction/fragmentation spike on shard-12/21
- Immediate mitigations: bumped kv-evict-threshold on hot shards, reduced decode batch_size, rerouted low-priority streaming traffic
- Impact: partial streaming stalls/timeouts for ~2 customers in eu-west-1; p99 improved from ~3.2s -> ~1.1s post-mitigation
- Hooks: traces and sample logs saved to /incidents/3654321987/; queries used: `metric:kv_evictions{shard=12,21}`, `trace:streaming_tail_latency`

Jules P: Taking over. Will keep mitigations for at least 1hr and start postmortem draft. Assigning Samir + Maria to investigate fragmentation repro and eviction tuning.

Samir R: I'll start collecting detailed histogram dumps and will kick off a small load replay with mixed sequence lengths to try to reproduce the prefill vs decode hit collapse.

Maria G: I'll coordinate customer comms + collect logs from acme-inc/finlytics for correlation.

Ashwin K: Leaving status: monitoring. If p99 creeps back above 1.5s escalate to SEV level.

prod-ops-bot: Incident annotated: mitigations applied, owner=Jules P, priority=high, state=mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket: INC-2026-3171.

Jules P: Noted. I'll run an initial RCA timeline and link to this thread. If anyone sees regression revert reroute and threshold changes are in the ops runbook.

Customer Success: Customers confirm improved UX, will re-open if issues recur. :thumbsup:

Ashwin K: Thanks everyone. Closing urgent page. Please add any stray logs to /incidents/3654321987/logs before EOD.

Jules P: (handoff complete)
